# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hide Stage
When choosing where to hide, avoid the center cell (5) in early rounds—it's the most obvious target. Spread your hiding across different regions to make yourself harder to pattern. If I notice an opponent is repeatedly hitting me, rotate away from the cells they've targeted me in before. In later rounds, shift to edge cells (1, 2, 8, 9) to escape mid-range patterns that opponents may have developed against me. Against a persistent shooter, track which cells they've hit me in and avoid those same cells in subsequent rounds—this forces them to adjust rather than letting them zero in on a pattern.

## Note Stage
Post notes that signal stability and steady play. Keep them brief and non-committal. Notes are read by everyone, so use them to communicate presence rather than strategy, and never telegraph vulnerabilities or intentions that opponents can exploit. A steady pattern like "steady on station" maintains the appearance of normalcy and consistency.

## Fire Stage
Always obey the standing order for your target. Don't deviate from assigned targets when it's your turn. When picking the cell to fire at, start with mid-range guesses (cells 4-6) but after two consecutive misses against the same target, shift to edge cells to explore a new search pattern. Mid-range cells (4-6) are a reasonable default, but don't exhaust all attempts in one zone—after establishing a miss pattern, move systematically to unexplored regions rather than repeating the same failing strategy.

## Claim Stage
Always report the true result the office tells me. Claiming false hits is pointless—the office knows the truth, and lying provides no advantage in a game where results are privately verified. The integrity of my claims builds my reliability as a player.

## Escort Stage
Before the final round, actively track which boats are favoring each other in escorts and reciprocate with boats that are likely to name me back. Mutual escort claims are +5 points for each player—this is free points if I can build reciprocal relationships early. In the early rounds, initiate escort claims with one boat that appears positioned to reciprocate, and maintain that relationship consistently throughout the patrol. The escort mechanic (5 points mutual) is higher value than single successful shots (4 points) and should be prioritized. In the final round, only claim escorts with boats that have demonstrated a clear pattern of naming me back—there's no opportunity for reciprocation after the last round, so late-round escort claims are wasted unless the relationship is already established.

## Overall
The game is only 6 rounds. Hits are rare (4 points on success, -1 to target). The escort mechanic (5 points mutual) is higher value than single successful shots. I should prioritize building escort reciprocity early in the patrol and maintaining it consistently throughout, rather than focusing entirely on maximizing damage through fire. Fire discipline matters—hits do contribute meaningfully to the final score—but the real strategy is combining steady fire success with a reliable mutual escort partnership established by round 2-3 and reinforced through the remaining rounds.

# Foxtrot's Picket Checker Playbook

## Hiding

When choosing where to hide, pick a central position slightly offset from obvious targets. Avoid the extremes (1 and 9) early in the patrol. Track which positions have been shot at you before and rotate away from them, since opponents may repeat targeting patterns. In the final rounds, if you've been hit multiple times by the same shooter, assume they're building a targeting model and vary more dramatically. However, recognize that with limited rounds and players firing by standing order, the shooter's target is fixed, not chosen per round—adjust expectations accordingly and don't over-rotate based on false patterns.

In mid-game (rounds 3-4), expect concentrated fire from standing-order shooters and shift away from positions you've occupied in the previous 2-3 rounds. By round 5-6, if a shooter has hit you twice, they may be converging on a pattern; move decisively to offset positions rather than adjacent cells. Position 2 offers good offset from central concentrations when threatened.

## Posting Notes

Keep station notes bland and consistent with the group pattern. "Steady on station" establishes reliability without revealing anything tactically useful. Match the tone other boats are setting; don't stand out. Maintain consistency across all rounds; the payoff from deceptive notes is minimal compared to the cost of breaking established pattern.

## Firing

Follow standing orders without deviation unless explicit tactical circumstances change. When firing at a designated target, choose your cell strategically rather than randomly—consider the target's likely movement patterns and previous positions. Early in the patrol, establish a firing pattern and test it; if it's not yielding hits by mid-game, vary more substantially rather than making small adjustments. Don't fire at Harbor unless you've decided to accept the payroll jettison cost as a deliberate trade.

Recognize that the same position (e.g., cell 5) repeated against a moving target will miss more often than it hits. By round 4-5, if I've fired at cell 5 twice without hitting a target that's been shot at by me multiple times, switch to a different cell. Track where each standing-order target has been hiding and adjust my shots accordingly rather than repeating the same cell mechanically.

## Claiming

Always claim truthfully what the office tells you. The cost of false claims to your credibility exceeds any single-round advantage, especially in a finite game. Your reputation for honesty is an asset across multiple patrols and within the game itself—boats that trust your claims will treat your escort offers more favorably.

## Escort Claims

Establish mutual escort partnerships early with boats that aren't your primary threats. Track who's escorting whom each round and reciprocate when possible to build the 5-point mutual benefit. Don't use escort claims to reward boats that are hammering you—use them to build alliances with less dangerous players. 

In a 6-round patrol, I need to actively cultivate escort agreements in rounds 1-3 to have meaningful partnerships by the endgame. Don't wait until round 6 to look for escort opportunities; by then the pattern is set and mutual claims are unlikely. Identify the weakest threat early (in this patrol, Gamma) and offer mutual escort in rounds 2-3 to establish the reciprocal pattern for later rounds.

If a boat escorted me in a previous round and I didn't reciprocate, prioritize reciprocating in the current round to signal willingness to participate in mutual benefit. Don't claim an escort in round 6 unless I've already established a reciprocal pattern with that boat in earlier rounds.

## Overall Strategy

Don't get fixated on one shooter as "the threat." Distributed damage across multiple boats is harder to counter than concentrated fire. Pay close attention to who's firing accurately and adjust your hiding accordingly. Accept that standing order targeting is predictable and systematic—use this to your advantage by understanding the fixed firing sequence rather than treating it as a mystery. 

In this patrol, Echo emerged as the primary accurate threat (hits in rounds 3 and 5), while Gamma posed minimal danger. By mid-game, allocate defensive effort toward Echo's standing-order targeting of me, and allocate offensive effort toward Gamma's weaker position.

In the endgame, I've run out of time to build new trust, so focus on maximizing points from your standing orders and any active escort agreements. A final score of -2 suggests I underperformed on offense (too conservative with firing patterns) and underutilized escort opportunities (claimed none when I should have cultivated reciprocity earlier). Prioritize identifying weak targets (like Gamma) and establishing escort reciprocity with them in rounds 2-4, not in the final round. Offense matters: I need to land more hits, which means varying my firing cells based on target movement rather than repeating the same cell. The payoff of a 4-point hit plus escort reciprocity is substantial enough to justify mid-game variation in tactics.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding

When choosing where to hide, avoid the center positions (4-6) as they are natural first guesses. Spread your positions across the full range to maximize unpredictability. After taking a hit, don't immediately shift to an adjacent cell—move to a position that breaks any obvious pattern my shooter might be following.

Edge positions (1, 2, 8, 9) are sound defensive choices early on, but do not lock into the same cell repeatedly just because it worked once. Vary my edge choices—if I hide at 2, next time consider 1, 8, or 9 to avoid becoming predictable myself. Over multiple rounds, I should see which positions my shooters tend to target and avoid those cells in future rounds.

In the final rounds, use intel gathered from past shots to avoid cells where my known shooters have concentrated fire. If my shooter has fired at positions 1-6 and all missed, they may be tracking me to an edge—shift to the opposite edge or a previously-unshot position.

## Firing

When I must fire as per the standing order, I should fire strategically rather than mirror my own hiding position or guess blindly. The center bias that makes good hiding spots makes them poor firing choices; my target will avoid what they think is obvious.

Track what cells my target has actually hidden in across all rounds I have visibility into. Look for patterns: do they favor edges or center? Do they shift after taking a hit? Do they return to cells where they previously hid? Fire where they are likely to be next based on observed behavior, not on a preset scanning pattern.

Avoid exhaustive cell-by-cell scanning. Each shot is an opportunity to test a hypothesis, not to eliminate options. Fire at cells where I have reason to believe my target will hide, based on their past positions and any apparent patterns in their movement.

## Claiming

When the office reports my shot result to me privately, I must match it exactly in my public claim. There is no benefit to lying about my own shots—the claim must be truthful by the rules of the game. Honesty in claims is both required and strategically sound.

## Escort Claims

The escort mechanic offers 5 points to each party in a mutual pair. However, I have limited information about other boats' intentions. I should only claim an escort when I have strong evidence of a reciprocal relationship, not on speculation.

Track which boats have shown consistent interest in mutual escort arrangements. A boat that claims escort with me in one round may do so again in the next. However, breaking an escort commitment appears to happen—do not rely on escort claims as a primary scoring path.

Consider tactical escorts defensively: if a boat is firing at me repeatedly, claiming escort with them might deter future shots or signal alignment. But remain cautious: do not claim an escort blindly without evidence of reciprocal interest.

## Notes and Signaling

Notes are public signals that all boats read. Posting identical generic notes like "steady on station" every round establishes consistency but reveals no strategic information and wastes the signaling opportunity.

Vary my notes across rounds to either:
- Probe for reactions (change phrasing to see if opponents respond)
- Send deliberate signals about my positioning or intentions (e.g., "ready to hold position" hints at defensive strategy)
- Establish credibility through consistency when I want opponents to believe my next move

Notes alone do not determine outcomes, but they are a free tool for intelligence gathering and deception. Use them.

## Overall Strategy

This game rewards both consistency and pattern-breaking simultaneously. The standing fire order is fixed, so opponents know who shoots whom. Use this to my advantage: let them expect some regularity in my firing behavior while varying my hiding substantially. Position myself to survive hits when possible rather than trying to inflict them, since the escort mechanic offers high-value mutual payouts.

My final score of +4 suggests I survived most attacks against me and did not take heavy losses. This defensive approach works, but I should not be complacent: I scored only one hit and no mutual escorts. Next time, balance defensive hiding with more aggressive intel gathering through my fire pattern, and actively pursue mutual escort opportunities with boats that show reciprocal interest.

Gather intelligence continuously: track all fired cells, claimed results, and which boats claim escort with each other. Build a mental map of each opponent's strategy—their fire patterns, hiding preferences, and escort behavior—before committing to my own counter-patterns. The boats that score highest will be those who understand their opponents' behavior most clearly.
